coverageDimensions: SERVICE coverage is the only dimension this page supplies, and it supplies it four times over — but the axis is "AWS managed application", which is narrower and messier than "AWS service". Of the 40 rows, several are features or sub-products rather than services: Amazon EKS Capabilities, Amazon Quick, AWS Transfer Family web apps, AWS account access (account access manager), Multi-party approval, OpenSearch user interface (Dashboards), Kiro. Several services appear more than once at different granularities — EMR occupies four rows (on EC2, on EKS, Serverless, Studio) and OpenSearch three (Service, Serverless, user interface). So 40 rows is 40 applications, not 40 services, and collapsing them to a service list is lossy in both directions. Denominator: the page gives no universe of all AWS services, so a percentage would need an external denominator and the page authorises none. REGION coverage: the page gives you nothing. It states a Region-shaped concept — "additional Regions of IAM Identity Center", with the Note that every listed application supports the primary Region — but it never names a single Region, never lists which additional Regions, and never says how many exist. The Region list lives behind the multi-region-iam-identity-center.md link, not here. Any Region count taken from this page is fabricated. RESOURCE TYPE coverage: the page gives you nothing. There is not one resource type, ARN, or CloudFormation type name anywhere on it. If a coverage map needs Region or resource-type dimensions for IAM Identity Center, this page cannot be the source for either.

features.featureName: AWS managed applications that integrate with IAM Identity Center (organization instances of IAM Identity Center)
features.reasoning: This is a real capability distinct from the four columns: an application either is an AWS managed application integrated with organization instances, or it is not. Its value set is the row list. The axis is external — Athena, Redshift, WorkSpaces, Glue, Lake Formation and the rest exist independently of IAM Identity Center; IAM Identity Center is not publishing a catalogue of its own objects here, it is reporting reach into a universe of other AWS offerings. Its truth is asserted in prose rather than in a cell, which is why it is easy to miss.
features.scope: Organization instances of IAM Identity Center
features.statuses: 40 covered, 2 not covered. Covered: table membership itself is the claim — the lead sentence states "All of the AWS managed applications in the following table integrate with organization instances of IAM Identity Center", so all 40 rows are Yes with no column to read. Not covered: the closing Note names Connect Customer and AWS Client VPN, which "are not listed in this table although you can use them with IAM Identity Center... because they integrate with IAM Identity Center exclusively using SAML and are therefore categorized as customer managed applications". Those two are stated exclusions from THIS capability, not from IAM Identity Center generally.

features.featureName: Integrated with account instances of IAM Identity Center
features.reasoning: A separate column means a separate list, so this is its own capability with its own Yes/No set — it is not a property of the organization-instance claim. The axis is the same external universe of AWS managed applications. The two footnotes are genuine partial support and must not be flattened into plain Yes.
features.scope: Account instances of IAM Identity Center
features.statuses: 29 Yes, 11 No, counted down column 2. No: Amazon Kendra, Amazon Managed Grafana, Amazon Monitron, Amazon SageMaker Studio, Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser, AWS account access (account access manager), AWS IoT Events, AWS IoT SiteWise, AWS Systems Manager, AWS Verified Access, Multi-party approval. Two of the 29 Yes values are footnote-qualified and are partial, not clean: Kiro (footnote 1 — account instances supported "unless your users require access to the full set of Kiro features on AWS websites") and Amazon Redshift (footnote 2 — supported "except for applications like Query Editor v2 that require permission sets, which are not supported by account instances").

features.featureName: Enables trusted identity propagation through IAM Identity Center
features.reasoning: Trusted identity propagation is a distinct IAM Identity Center feature with its own supported-application list, and the column disagrees with the others row by row (SageMaker Studio is No for account instances but Yes here; WorkSpaces is the reverse), which proves the lists are independent. External axis, same reason as above.
features.statuses: 25 Yes, 15 No, counted down column 3. No: Amazon CodeCatalyst, Amazon Kendra, Amazon Managed Grafana, Amazon Monitron, Amazon WorkSpaces, Amazon WorkSpaces Secure Browser, AWS App Studio, AWS Deadline Cloud, AWS IoT Events, AWS IoT SiteWise, AWS re:Post Private, AWS Supply Chain, AWS Systems Manager, AWS Transform, AWS Verified Access. No footnotes attach to this column.

features.featureName: Supports IAM Identity Center configured with a customer managed KMS key
features.reasoning: Encryption support is its own list and its own column. The axis stays the external application universe. The icon/text conflict makes this the one column where a parser must choose a source of truth; the text wins because the page's Note independently confirms the text on the rows where the two disagree and can be checked.
features.scope: Encryption at rest with a customer managed KMS key
features.statuses: 37 Yes, 3 No by the cell TEXT, which is the reading I take. No: AWS App Studio, AWS IoT Events, AWS IoT SiteWise. Six rows are internally inconsistent in the Markdown — the cell renders a negative_icon image but the text beside it reads "Yes": Amazon EMR Serverless, Amazon Managed Grafana, Amazon Redshift, Amazon SageMaker Studio, Amazon WorkSpaces, AWS Deadline Cloud. The page's own Note resolves three of the six: "Applications that support deployment in additional Regions of IAM Identity Center also support IAM Identity Center configured with a customer managed KMS key" — EMR Serverless, Redshift and Deadline Cloud are all Yes in the additional-Regions column, so their KMS value must be Yes and the icon is wrong. Reading the icon instead would give 31 Yes / 9 No and contradict the page's stated rule.

features.featureName: Supports deployment in additional Regions of IAM Identity Center
features.reasoning: The column is a fourth independent list over the same external application axis. Crucially the VALUES are still applications: the column tells you which applications can be deployed in additional Regions, and names not one Region. Treating it as a Region axis would invent data the page does not contain.
features.scope: Additional (non-primary) Regions of IAM Identity Center — the primary Region is universal and out of scope
features.statuses: 14 Yes, 26 No, counted down column 4. Yes: Amazon Athena SQL, Amazon EMR on EC2, Amazon EMR on EKS, Amazon EMR Serverless, Amazon EMR Studio, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3 Access Grants, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, AWS Deadline Cloud, AWS DevOps Agent, AWS Glue, AWS Lake Formation, AWS Systems Manager, AWS Transfer Family web apps. One Yes is scoped, not whole-service: AWS Systems Manager reads "Yes - Fleet Manager Remote Desktop", so only that capability of Systems Manager is covered. One No is footnoted: AWS account access (account access manager) is No with footnote 3, "You enable account access manager in the primary Region of IAM Identity Center". The Note also states every listed application supports the primary Region, so a No here means primary-Region-only, never no support at all.

pageTitle: AWS managed applications that you can use with IAM Identity Center
shouldNotExtract: The "See also" section in full, including the appended AI-coding-assistant boilerplate about `aws agent-toolkit search-skills --search-query singlesignon` — that is AWS page furniture, not a capability, and the CLI command is not a value on any axis. The four bullets under the intro that preview the table columns are a description of the table, not a separate list of four covered things. The cross-reference links (organization-instances-identity-center.md, account-instances-identity-center.md, trustedidentitypropagation-overview.md, encryption-at-rest.md, multi-region-iam-identity-center.md, multi-region-application-use.md, customermanagedapps.md, the Kiro User Guide link, the account-access-manager IAM guide link) are navigation. The success_icon.png / negative_icon.png image URLs are rendering artifacts, not data. The two Notes are qualifying prose: mine them for the primary-Region and KMS-implication rules, but do not emit them as coverage rows. There are no quotas, prices, prerequisites, code examples, or troubleshooting on this page to guard against.
trap: Three traps, in order of likely damage. First, the customer managed KMS key column is self-contradictory in six rows — the cell holds a negative_icon image with the word "Yes" next to it (Amazon EMR Serverless, Amazon Managed Grafana, Amazon Redshift, Amazon SageMaker Studio, Amazon WorkSpaces, AWS Deadline Cloud). A parser keying on the icon filename gets 31/40; a parser keying on the text gets 37/40. The text is right: the page's own Note says anything supporting additional Regions also supports a customer managed KMS key, and EMR Serverless, Redshift and Deadline Cloud are all Yes for additional Regions, so their negative icons are simply wrong. Second, the "additional Regions" column looks like Region coverage and is not — its values are applications, it names zero Regions, and a No means primary-Region-only rather than unsupported, because the Note says every listed application supports the primary Region. Reading it as "26 applications have no Region support" inverts the meaning. Third, a careless parser reads the page as one capability with 40 supported services, when it is five: the four columns disagree with each other row by row, the organization-instance claim lives only in prose above the table, the footnoted Yes values for Kiro and Amazon Redshift are partial support and not clean Yes, AWS Systems Manager's Region Yes is scoped to Fleet Manager Remote Desktop only, and the two explicit exclusions (Connect Customer, AWS Client VPN) sit in a closing Note rather than in any row.
whatThePageStates: The page lists the AWS managed applications that an administrator can grant access to through IAM Identity Center without separate federation or user/group synchronisation. Its body is a single matrix: 40 named AWS managed applications down the side, and 4 capability columns across the top (account instances, trusted identity propagation, customer managed KMS key, deployment in additional Regions), each cell carrying an explicit Yes or No. Prose above the table adds a fifth claim that every listed application integrates with organization instances of IAM Identity Center, three numbered footnotes qualify individual cells, and a closing note names two AWS services deliberately kept off the table because they integrate by SAML only.
